digest.component_or_area: LLM verifier model resolution across review kernel, completion, and workflow gates
propositions: Three independent code paths select the verifier model and each breaks off the default provider via equality tests against DEFAULT_MODEL, causing non-default class configurations to silently revert to the frontier model.

code-review.yaml's verify step declares no model: key and falls through to cfg.model, running on the frontier model instead of the configured standard class, and temperature: 0 for greedy Pass-2 determinism never takes effect.
Provider-qualified model strings (e.g., anthropic:claude-opus-4-8) defeat string equality heuristics, so changing providers silently keeps verification on the old provider's model.

All three verifier paths must call resolve_model_string() to map class names (trivial/standard/frontier) to their configured model ids, replacing the equality-test pattern with a single reserved-word vocabulary.

The resolution mechanism cannot use a single module-level interception point because model_classes imports config at module scope and forbids the reverse, requiring lazy function-level imports instead.
